Q5672.reason: Acquittal on insanity grounds is personal to the shooter, so the defendant (who is an accessory) can still be convicted; it doesn't negate that the killing was an unlawful act, though the defendant's liability remains, and among the options only insanity is a personal excuse—so the defendant could argue the principal's acquittal is no bar; self-defense would be a justification that negates the crime.
